coreInvariants.name: Bank conservation
coreInvariants.statement: totalUnclaimableOf[t] == SUM over u of unclaimablePromoOf[t][u], for every token t
coreInvariants.evidence: Exhaustive write-site enumeration. Only two mutation sites: batchClaim :479-480 increments BOTH by the same `pending`; claimUnclaimablePromo :564-565 zeroes the user entry and decrements the total by exactly `amount` (never wholesale-zeroed). finalizePromotion :527-528 deliberately does NOT clear either mapping. No other writes exist.

coreInvariants.name: Flushing implies paused
coreInvariants.evidence: Flushing is set only at beginFlush :436, immediately after _pause() :433. The sole _unpause() call site is :282 inside unpause(), which reverts while Flushing (:281). Therefore no path clears the pause while Flushing. This is what makes _claimRewards' promo settlement (:870-876, gated only on promoToken != 0, NOT on phase) unreachable during a flush — its callers stake/withdraw/claim are all whenNotPaused (:643,:688,:738).

coreInvariants.name: accPromoPerShare frozen during Flushing
coreInvariants.statement: promoPhase == Flushing ==> accPromoPerShare does not advance
coreInvariants.evidence: _updatePool's accrual block is gated `address(promoToken) != address(0) && promoPhase != PromoPhase.Flushing` at :824. This is the story-024 / audit-07 H-01 fix, enforced at the accrual site rather than via whenNotPaused on callers, which closes the three paths that reach _updatePool while paused (collectReward, setDesiredAPY commit branch, setDepletionDuration) — see the rationale comment :813-823. beginFlush's own final accrual (:432) runs while phase is still Active, so it is unaffected. The pendingPromo view mirrors the same gate at :955-958, so view and state agree.

coreInvariants.name: accPromoPerShare never reset
coreInvariants.statement: accPromoPerShare is monotonically non-decreasing across promotions
coreInvariants.evidence: finalizePromotion clears promoToken/rate/balance (:524-526) but deliberately not the accumulator (:497-499). Only write site is the += at :829. Combined with batchClaim's unconditional debt alignment (:468), pending against the next token starts at exactly zero.

coreInvariants.name: Flush completeness over a frozen set
coreInvariants.statement: finalizePromotion requires flushCursor == _stakers.length(), and set membership cannot mutate during the flush
coreInvariants.evidence: Requirement at :513. _stakers mutates only at stake :672 (whenNotPaused) and withdraw :718 (whenNotPaused); INV-2 gives paused during Flushing, so the set is frozen. flushCursor advances monotonically (:460-486) making coverage contiguous. pauseWithdraw (:596, whenPaused) deliberately does NOT touch membership (:592-594).

coreInvariants.name: Sweep reserves the bank
coreInvariants.statement: finalizePromotion never transfers out tokens owed to the per-user bank
coreInvariants.evidence: leftover = balance > banked ? balance - banked : 0 at :517-519, saturating deliberately so the function can never revert and pin the contract in Flushing (:506-509). Contrast the pre-change behaviour at 7045a96:src/PhlimboV3.sol:495, where the global scalar `unclaimablePromo` was zeroed and its tokens swept as leftover — this is the audit-08 M-01 fix.

invariantsNOTVerified.statement: promoToken.balanceOf(this) >= totalUnclaimableOf[promoToken] (bank solvency for the LIVE token)
invariantsNOTVerified.why: Requires reasoning over the interleaving of _claimRewards' reverting promo settlement (:873, pays from accrued amounts tracked via promoRewardBalance) against banked amounts (tracked separately in totalUnclaimableOf). The two accounting systems are disjoint and never cross-checked. Cannot be discharged by local static reasoning — needs a Tier-3 invariant/fuzz run. NOT a claim that it is violated; it is simply not locally provable.
invariantsNOTVerified.recommendation: Hand to invariant-generator as a candidate invariant.

invariantsNOTVerified.statement: Re-using a previously-retired token as a NEW promo token is safe w.r.t. its surviving bank
invariantsNOTVerified.why: startPromotion (:356) rejects only address(0)/phUSD/rewardToken — it does NOT reject a token whose bank from an earlier promotion is still outstanding. On re-use the contract already holds `banked` of that token while promoRewardBalance tracks only the new `amount` (:369). finalizePromotion's reservation is cumulative over totalUnclaimableOf[token] (:517) so it appears self-consistent, and emergencyTransfer's live-token sweep (:335-340) would again reach that bank. Flagged for interaction/econ scanners to adjudicate; not adjudicated here.

invariantsNOTVerified.status: violated (as literally stated in the code comment)
invariantsNOTVerified.why: The comment at :670-671 asserts membership <=> amount > 0. The forward direction (amount > 0 ==> member) holds. The converse does NOT survive pauseWithdraw: :596-611 can drive user.amount to 0 while deliberately leaving membership intact (:592-594). The weaker true invariant is `amount > 0 ==> member`. The code's own design accounts for this (a zero-amount member is visited by the flush with pending == 0, harmless per :594), so this is a documentation imprecision, not a behavioural defect. Recorded so downstream agents do not rely on the stronger biconditional.

localFindings.description: emergencyTransfer ends with _pause(). OpenZeppelin's Pausable._pause() carries `whenNotPaused` (Pausable.sol:96), so it REVERTS when the contract is already paused. Consequently emergencyTransfer is not callable while the contract is paused — which includes the whole Flushing window (INV-2) and any ordinary pause. Surfaced as a grounded behavioural fact only; exploitability/severity is deliberately not adjudicated here. NOTE for triage: the project's established position is that emergencyTransfer/pauseWithdraw are terminal 'ejector seats' by design (see prior-run precedent pe7m2, closed INVALID).
localFindings.recommendation: No recommendation made at profile stage — for code-scanner to adjudicate against the ejector-seat precedent.

localFindings.description: `uint256 end = cursor + maxIterations;` overflows and reverts (checked arithmetic) for maxIterations near type(uint256).max, rather than clamping. The clamp at :456-458 only handles end > len after the addition. Fails closed (revert), permissionless caller, no state written — recorded for completeness, not a DoS (any other value works).
